questions.stem:
A particle, P, of mass 0.5 kg is moving along the positive x-axis. At time t seconds, $t \geqslant 0$, P is x metres from the origin O and is moving away from O with velocity $v\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, where $v = \frac{1}{(4x+3)}$

When $t = 0$, P is at O.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the distance of P from O when $t = 2$
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
$v = \frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{1}{(4x+3)}$
$\frac{dt}{dx} = 4x+3$
$t = \int (4x+3)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\times 4x^2+3x+c$
OR $\int_0^2 dt = \int_0^X (4x+3)\,dx = \left[\frac{1}{2}\times 4x^2+3x\right]_0^X$
M1,dM1A1: Rewrite as $\frac{dx}{dt}$ and separate variables to reach a form ready for integration (M1); attempt the integration (at least one power going up) (dM1); correct integration, constant/limits not needed (A1)
$c=0$
$t=2=\frac{1}{2}\times 4x^2+3x$, $2x^2+3x-2=0$ dM1: Use $t=2$ in their expression or substitute correct limits, and solve their 3 term quadratic to find $x$. If solving an incorrect quadratic, evidence of a correct method must be seen. Depends on the previous M mark.
$x=\frac{1}{2}$ ($x=-2$) A1cso: Obtain $x=\frac{1}{2}$ (and reject $-2$ if seen) from completely correct work. Constant of integration must have been seen, although we do not need to see evidence of evaluation.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the magnitude of the resultant force acting on P when $t = 2$
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
$a = v\frac{dv}{dx}$ alt: $a = \frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{1}{2}v^2\right)$ M1: Use $a = v\frac{dv}{dx}$
$=\frac{1}{4x+3}\times\frac{-4}{(4x+3)^2}$ dM1A1: Differentiate the given expression for $v$ and obtain an expression for $a$. We need to see a power of 2 (or a power of 3 if using $\frac{d}{dx}(\frac{1}{2}v^2)$). Depends on the previous M mark. (A1: Correct expression, any form.)
$|F| = \frac{1}{2}\times\frac{4}{(2+3)^3} = \frac{2}{125} = 0.016\,\mathrm{N}$ M1 A1cso: Use their acceleration in an equation of motion to obtain a value for $F$. Mass must be included and they must use their value of $x$. Independent, but must have found an expression for acceleration. A1cso: Correct magnitude of $F$. Correct solution only. Can be fraction or decimal. Must be positive.
